title: Chandra Pal Singh v. State of U.P. (bill correction relegated to cl. 6.5)
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pankaj Naqvi, J.; Piyush Agrawal, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; bill-correction claim relegated to Regulation 6.5.
headnote: A writ seeking correction of a domestic electricity bill was disposed of without examining the bill on merits. The Court accepted that the appropriate remedy is a representation to the competent authority under Regulation 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, who shall consider the claim forthwith.
facts: Chandra Pal Singh invoked the writ jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court seeking a mandamus to respondent no. 3 to correct the electricity bill issued against his domestic connection no. 771718264559. Counsel for the petitioner, the Power Corporation, and the State were heard. The Corporation submitted that the competent authority under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, not the writ court, was the forum for the bill-correction claim.

holding_units.holding: A writ of mandamus seeking correction of a domestic electricity bill is not the appropriate forum; the consumer must approach the competent authority under Regulation 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, who shall consider the claim forthwith.

principle_tags.application: The Court disposed of the writ for bill correction by relegating the petitioner to the competent authority under Regulation 6.5, without deciding the bill on merits.
The Power Corporation's submission that Regulation 6.5 is the appropriate remedy for the bill-correction claim was accepted as correct and the petition was ordered accordingly.

not_decided.point: correctness of the domestic electricity bill
not_decided.note: Merits of the bill-correction claim were not examined; the petitioner was relegated to Regulation 6.5.
